To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the p53 protein is overexpressed in 40-50% of breast cancers and is an independent prognostic marker of poor outcome.
the expression of c-erbB-2 and p53 proteins in breast cancer patients is associated with poor prognosis.
(a) the expression of c-erbB-2 is associated with the prognosis of breast cancer; and (b) the expression of p53 and the co-expression of p53 and c-erb-B2 are also associated with the prognosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the expression of p53 protein, c-erbB-2, and their prognostic significance in breast carcinoma.
the prognostic value of the coexpression in breast cancer of p53 and c-erb B2 proteins.
the development of new, more effective and less toxic drugs for the treatment of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53 protein overexpression is a poor prognostic factor for patients with primary breast carcinoma, whereas p53 mutations are not associated with a poor prognosis.
there is no evidence to support a role for p53 in the pathogenesis of breast cancer.
the coexpression of c-erbB-2 and p53 is not an independent prognostic factor in breast cancer, but it might have some prognostic significance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p53 and c-erb-2 protein co-expression is associated with a poor prognosis in patients with breast cancer, regardless of the histologic type.
the coexpression of the p53 protein and the c-erbB-2 protein in breast carcinoma is associated with a poor prognosis.
the coexpression of the p53 protein and C-erbb2 is an independent prognostic indicator in breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p53 and c-erb B-2 proteins may be useful prognostic markers in breast cancer.
there is a strong correlation between the expression of p53 and c-erb B2 in breast cancer and that the coexpression of these two proteins is a strong predictor of poor survival.
we have shown that there is a correlation between the coexpression of c-erbB-2 and p53 and the development of breast cancer in women.
